group.title: Weather and seasons
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: When water falls from the sky.
examples: Take an umbrella. It’s going to {rain}.
wrong: It rained all day, so the ground was dry.

words.meaning: When soft white ice falls from the sky.
examples: It {snows} a lot here in winter.
wrong: It snowed, so the beach was hot and sunny.

words.meaning: Thick gray air near the ground that is hard to see through.
examples: I can’t see the road in this {fog}.
wrong: The fog was so clear we could see for miles.

words.meaning: A little cold, but nice.
examples: It’s a {cool} evening, so bring a sweater.
wrong: It was cool, so the ice cream melted in a second.

words.meaning: The light and heat that come from the sun.
examples: We sat outside in the {sunshine}.
wrong: We stood in the sunshine in the dark night.

words.meaning: Very, very cold.
examples: Wear a coat. It’s {freezing} outside!
wrong: It’s freezing, so let’s go swimming in the sea.

words.meaning: A strong shoe that covers your foot and part of your leg.
examples: Wear your {boots} in the snow.
wrong: I wear my boots on my hands.

words.meaning: A coat that keeps you dry in the rain.
examples: Put on your {raincoat}. It’s wet outside.
wrong: I wear a raincoat to stay wet.

words.meaning: Cold in a way that is not nice.
examples: It’s {chilly} this morning.
wrong: It was chilly, so I took off my coat to warm up.

words.meaning: A figure of a person that children make out of snow.
examples: The kids made a {snowman} in the garden.
wrong: We made a snowman on the hot beach in July.

words.meaning: A ball you make out of snow.
examples: He threw a {snowball} at his brother.
wrong: I threw a snowball made of sand.

words.meaning: A small pool of water on the ground after rain.
examples: The boy jumped in a {puddle}.
wrong: The puddle was full of dry sand.

words.meaning: Dark glasses that keep bright light out of your eyes.
examples: It’s sunny. Where are my {sunglasses}?
wrong: I wear sunglasses to see better in the dark.

words.meaning: A hat with a wide edge that keeps the sun off your face.
examples: Wear a {sun hat} at the beach.
wrong: I wear a sun hat to keep my feet warm.

words.meaning: A report that tells you if it will be sunny, rainy or cold.
examples: The {weather forecast} says it will rain.
wrong: The weather forecast told us yesterday’s news.

words.meaning: Very, very hot.
examples: It’s {boiling} today. Let’s go swimming.
wrong: It was boiling, so we wore hats and gloves.

words.meaning: Short pants that stop above the knee.
examples: I wear {shorts} when it’s hot.
wrong: I wear shorts to keep my legs warm in the snow.

words.meaning: An open shoe for hot weather.
examples: She wore {sandals} at the beach.
wrong: I wear sandals to keep my feet dry in the snow.

words.meaning: One small drop of rain.
examples: A {raindrop} fell on my nose.
wrong: A raindrop fell up into the sky.

words.meaning: One small, soft piece of snow.
examples: A {snowflake} landed on my hand.
wrong: The snowflake was hot and black.

words.meaning: Covered with ice, or very cold.
examples: Be careful. The road is {icy}.
wrong: The icy road was hot and dry.

words.meaning: A storm with loud noise, bright light in the sky and rain.
examples: We stayed inside during the {thunderstorm}.
wrong: The thunderstorm was quiet and sunny.

words.meaning: Red, painful skin from too much sun.
examples: I got a {sunburn} at the beach.
wrong: I got a sunburn from the snow at night.

words.meaning: A thing that shows how hot or cold it is.
examples: The {thermometer} says it’s ten degrees.
wrong: I use a thermometer to tell the time.

words.meaning: Clean, cool air from outside.
examples: Open the window for some {fresh air}.
wrong: I went into the dark box to get some fresh air.

words.meaning: A question to ask if it is sunny, rainy or cold.
examples: {What’s the weather like} in Paris today?
wrong: "What’s the weather like?" I asked, to find out his name.

words.meaning: The season after summer, when leaves drop from trees.
examples: The leaves turn red in the {fall}.
wrong: Fall is the hottest part of summer.

words.meaning: A lot of rain falling fast.
examples: {Heavy rain} made the roads wet.
wrong: The heavy rain was just two small drops.

words.meaning: Colder than the point where water turns to ice.
examples: In winter it is often {below zero}.
wrong: It was below zero, so we swam in the lake.

words.meaning: A machine that makes a room warm.
examples: Turn on the {heater}. It’s cold.
wrong: I turned on the heater to make the room cold.

words.meaning: Clothes you wear to swim.
examples: Don’t forget your {swimsuit} for the beach.
wrong: I wore my swimsuit to the snow party in the mountains.

words.meaning: A small flat thing you sit on to slide down snow.
examples: The kids rode a {sled} down the hill.
wrong: We rode the sled down the hot, dry road.

words.meaning: A warm glove with one part for the thumb and one for the fingers.
examples: Put on your {mittens}. It’s snowing.
wrong: I wear mittens on my feet in summer.

words.meaning: A machine that makes the air in a room cool.
examples: The {air conditioning} keeps the office cool.
wrong: We turned on the air conditioning to make the room hot.

words.meaning: To have water or rain fall on you.
examples: Take an umbrella or you’ll {get wet}.
wrong: I stood in the rain and didn’t get wet at all.

words.meaning: Cold, rain, wind or storms.
examples: The game stopped because of {bad weather}.
wrong: The bad weather was warm, sunny and calm.

words.meaning: A storm with a lot of snow and wind.
examples: The school closed because of the {snowstorm}.
wrong: The snowstorm made the beach hot and sunny.

words.meaning: Thick things to wear that keep you from getting cold.
examples: Bring {warm clothes} for the mountains.
wrong: I wore warm clothes to feel cold.

words.meaning: A soft, warm hat for cold days.
examples: Wear your {wool hat} in the snow.
wrong: I wear a wool hat to keep cool in summer.

words.meaning: A day when it rains a lot.
examples: On a {rainy day} we play games inside.
wrong: On a rainy day the sun shines and the ground is dry.
